design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the varicella zoster vaccine group or placebo group using a random number table generated by an independent epidemiologist.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation was generated using a random number table by an independent epidemiologist, concealed by pharmacy staff, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent epidemiologist generated a series of randomization codes for varicella zoster vaccine solution or distilled water based on a random number table. Independent research staff at the hospital pharmacy were then informed of the codes. Pharmacists produced a vaccine solution or purified distilled water that were identical in appearance. A member of the medical staff was informed of the allocated participant code according to the order in the code table, but was blinded to the contents of the codes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and administering medical personnel were effectively blinded using identical-appearing placebos, and an intention-to-treat analysis was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled study of 60– 70-year-old people with diabetes was conducted to ascertain the safety and immunogenicity of varicella zoster vaccine... Pharmacists produced a vaccine solution or purified distilled water that were identical in appearance. A member of the medical staff was informed of the allocated participant code according to the order in the code table, but was blinded to the contents of the codes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 52 of 54 participants (96.3%), missingness was minimal and balanced, and primary analyses included all 54 participants via intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 54 receiving the study vaccine were included in the ITT analysis set. During follow-up, one participant was unable to visit the hospital and another died of acute cardiac insufficiency (heart failure) that was wholly unrelated to the vaccination. Consequently, 52 (96.2%) participants were included in the per-protocol analysis set.

domain_judgments.rationale: Standardized outcome measures (skin test, ELISPOT, IAHA antibody assays) were used, and outcome assessors were blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A member of the medical staff was informed of the allocated participant code according to the order in the code table, but was blinded to the contents of the codes... The primary outcome measure was the change in cell-mediated immunity at 3 months after vaccination, as measured by the varicella skin test reaction.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (UMIN000004771) and all pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes were reported according to the planned analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered with the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, Japan (UMIN000004771)... The primary outcome measure was the change in cell-mediated immunity at 3 months after vaccination, as measured by the varicella skin test reaction. Secondary outcomes included cell-mediated immunity measured using an interferon–c (IFN–c) enzyme-linked immunospot (ELISPOT) assay and immune adherence haemagglutination (IAHA) titres to VZV 3 months after vaccination.

overall_summary: The study was a well-conducted double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial with adequate allocation concealment, blinding of participants and staff, minimal missing outcome data, and pre-registered outcome reporting, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial in which participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two vaccination sequences.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were randomized 1:1 stratified by years since prior HZ, but specific details on allocation sequence generation and concealment were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 101 subjects, 50 years of age with a history of HZ 5 years prior to screening, were enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two vaccination groups. Enrollment in each group was stratified in an approximate 2:1 ratio by number of years since their episode of HZ

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with indistinguishable placebo, and participants followed their assigned crossover intervention sequence without reported substantial deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Vaccine and placebo were reconstituted with sterile diluent immediately prior to administration, and were indistinguishable from each other.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for nearly all randomized participants (only 1 of 101 subjects withdrew).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: As shown in Fig. 1, 100% (51/51) of the subjects randomized to Group 1 and 98.0% (49/50) of subjects randomized to Group 2 completed all study visits. After randomization, one subject in Group 2 was discontinued from the study after withdrawing consent prior to receipt of zoster vaccine at dose 2.

domain_judgments.rationale: Immunogenicity outcomes were objectively measured via gpELISA, and clinical adverse events were captured using standardized Vaccination Report Cards while treatment allocation was double-blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blood samples were drawn on day 1, week 4, and week 8 postenrollment and tested for VZV antibody titer by gpELISA.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT00322231) and results for all stated primary safety and secondary immunogenicity outcomes are consistently reported according to the prespecified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary objective was to determine whether zoster vaccine was generally well tolerated when administered to HZ history-positive adults 50 years of age. The secondary objective was to determine whether zoster vaccine was immunogenic when administered to HZ history-positive adults.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to insufficient reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment methods in Domain 1, despite low risk across all other domains.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either zoster vaccine or placebo using a computer-generated, study-center-specific allocation schedule.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, centrally managed, concealed by sequential assignment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive 2 doses of either ZV or placebo, according to a computer-generated, study-center specific allocation schedule... Allocation numbers were assigned sequentially by the study site personnel to subjects who met the study eligibility criteria, beginning with the lowest number available at the study center, after informed consent and medical history had been obtained. The allocation schedule was generated by a sponsor statistician not otherwise associated with the ZV program.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was maintained through an unblinded vaccine coordinator using opaque labels without contact with participants, and there were no deviations from the intended protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The subject, investigator, clinical study site personnel, and sponsor personnel directly involved in the study were blinded to whether the subject received zoster vaccine or placebo... The clinical materials were prepared by an unblinded vaccine coordinator at each clinical site, because of differences in the turbidity of the study vaccine and placebo... wrapped the syringe in an opaque label... did not have any contact with the subject and did not disclose the contents of the syringe to the person administering the study vaccine/placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: While overall safety follow-up was high, the primary immunogenicity endpoints were analyzed per-protocol with substantial attrition (e.g. 68/104 in ZV and 72/105 in placebo at 6 weeks postdose 2) without clear demonstration that missingness was unrelated to outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Almost all subjects randomized to both treatment groups received two doses of ZV or placebo and had safety follow-up for 42 days after the second vaccination (Fig. 1). One subject in the ZV group was randomized, but not vaccinated, and was not included in the analyses. After receiving at least 1 dose of ZV or placebo, 7 subjects in the ZV group and 7 subjects in the placebo group were discontinued.

domain_judgments.rationale: Immunogenicity assays were objective laboratory measurements conducted in a blinded manner at a central laboratory using validated assays.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Immunogenicity was evaluated using VZV interferon-gamma (IFN--) enzyme-linked immunospot (ELISPOT) assay and VZV glycoprotein enzyme-linked immunosorbent antibody (gpELISA) assay... PBMC were frozen, stored in liquid nitrogen freezer, shipped encased in dry ice to a central laboratory, and then stored in a liquid nitrogen freezer until testing in a validated IFN-- ELISPOT assay.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT00109122), and reported predefined primary and secondary immunogenicity and safety endpoints according to a prespecified statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study (NCT00109122) examined the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity after 1 and 2 doses of ZV in adults 60 years of age and older... The primary immunogenicity endpoints were the VZV IFN-- ELISPOT geometric mean counts (GMCs) at 6 weeks after each dose of ZV. The analyses were performed by estimating the ratios of the VZV IFN-- ELISPOT GMCs between the 2 vaccination groups at 6 weeks after each dose of ZV using a longitudinal regression model adjusting for prevaccination VZV IFN-- ELISPOT count, age, and study center.

overall_summary: The study was well-conducted and double-blinded with proper allocation concealment, but some concerns exist regarding missing outcome data due to the per-protocol immunogenicity analysis where up to 35% of participants were excluded at certain time points.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial evaluating the VZV vaccine versus placebo in 38,546 adults aged 60 years or older.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were randomly assigned in a double-blind, placebo-controlled design coordinated through the VA Cooperative Studies Program, and baseline characteristics between the two study groups were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We conducted a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial at 22 sites, in which adults 60 years of age or older received either VZV vaccine or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical placebo, blinding was well-maintained, and a modified intention-to-treat approach excluding only early cases was corroborated by sensitivity analyses including all cases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy analyses were performed with the use of a follow-up interval that excluded the first 30 days after vaccination and the modified intention-to-treat population, which excluded subjects who withdrew or in whom a confirmed case of herpes zoster developed within the first 30 days after vaccination... The results were essentially unchanged when subjects in whom herpes zoster developed during the first 30 days were included.

domain_judgments.rationale: More than 95% of participants completed surveillance with balanced, extremely low rates of withdrawal and loss to follow-up (0.6%) across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: More than 95 percent of the subjects continued in the study to its completion, with a median of 3.12 years of surveillance for herpes zoster... Only 0.6 percent of the subjects withdrew from the study or were lost to follow-up; 4.1 percent died during the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Suspected cases were assessed using objective laboratory PCR assays and blinded adjudicators, and pain questionnaires were administered uniformly under blinded conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Before unblinding, each suspected case of herpes zoster was classified as a confirmed case of herpes zoster or as not a confirmed case with the use of a hierarchical algorithm that incorporated the results of the polymerase-chain-reaction (PCR) assay performed at the central laboratory of the study, virus culture at the local virology laboratory, and the final clinical diagnosis of the study's clinical evaluation committee...

domain_judgments.rationale: The analysis followed a detailed pre-specified statistical analysis plan published and established before database unblinding, with all primary and secondary endpoints reported fully as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A data-analysis plan was completed before the data were unblinded for analysis. The analysis was performed by the VACSP coordinating center (West Haven, Conn.), with review and approval by the executive committee of the study.

overall_summary: The study is a rigorously conducted, large-scale, double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial with minimal loss to follow-up, objective and blinded outcome ascertainment, and pre-specified analyses, yielding a low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains.
